subject.title: feat(memory-lancedb): scope memory_recall and memory_forget + configurable thresholds

question: Should the official memory-lancedb plugin adopt caller-controlled scope partitions now, or wait for a trusted session-bound scope model?
rationale: The branch introduces new model-facing tool behavior, persistent schema, configuration defaults, and a partition primitive that is deliberately not an authorization boundary; code review cannot choose that permanent product and upgrade contract.

options.title: Narrow the contract first
options.body: Define structured scope input for all memory tools, keep tenant/security claims out, remove unrelated provenance, and require a versioned migration before merging.

options.title: Accept caller partitions
options.body: Approve the current caller-controlled partition model as an official convenience feature and explicitly own its non-security-boundary and upgrade tradeoffs.

options.title: Defer to specialized plugins
options.body: Keep the official plugin lean and direct operators needing multi-scope memory to a maintained specialized plugin until a trusted core/plugin scope signal exists.

recommendation.title: Narrow the contract first
recommendation.body: Define structured scope input for all memory tools, keep tenant/security claims out, remove unrelated provenance, and require a versioned migration before merging.

likelyOwner.reason: Recent merge and refactor history makes this the best available owner for the official plugin's product and upgrade contract.
